sentences.text: The petitioner is the licensee of a canteen and light refreshment stall at the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation Bus stand at Aluva.

entities.text: Kerala State Road Transport Corporation Bus stand
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has been conducting the said canteen and stall pursuant to a licence issued by the first respondent.
As per Exhibit P1, his licence was renewed for a period of one year from 01.04.2013 to 31.03.2014.
Therefore, the term of his licence expires today.
According to the petitioner, the licence used to be renewed on the previous occasions, on the licensee remitting licence fee at a rate 10% in excess of the license fee of the previous year.
It is contended that, Exhibit P5 is the memorandum that containss the terms and conditions subject to which the licence was granted.
The petitioner has remitted the license fee for the entire period.

He also has been issued with the requisite licencee under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006,
which is valid up to 31.03.2014.
The petitioner has been conducting the canteen for the past six years.
According to him, there has been no cause for any complaint against the establishment from anyone, till date.
However, in spite of the above by Exhibit P4, the petitioner has been informed that the licence in respect of the canteen could not be renewed in his favour for the period after 31.03.2014.

The petitioner has filed this writ petition aggrieved by Exhibit P4.
2.

According to the counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner has a vested right that has been recognized by Clause-3 of Exhibit R3(a), which according to the respondents is the memorandum that governs the transaction.
Therefore, the petitioner has a right to insist that the licence be renewed in his favour provided he pays license fee at a rate 10% in excess of the rate for the previous year.
The petitioner is willing to do so.
Therefore, it is contended that the refusal to renew his licence is without any justification.

The petitioner also alleges that, at the instance of the office bearers of recognized trade unions of the employees, unreasonable demands for money had been made, which the petitioner had refused to satisfy, thereby antagonizing them.
Exhibit P4 has been issued, at their instance, it is contended.
3. Advocate Babu Joseph Kuruvathazha appears for the respondents.
A counter affidavit has been filed by the third respondent.
According to the counsel, Clause-3 of Exhibit R3(a) stipulates the submission of an application seeking renewal of the licence, two months before the date of expiry of the term of licence.

It is pointed out that the petitioner's application referred to in Exhibit P3 is Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/
3 dated 04.03.2014.

entities.text: Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, the said application was not submitted within the time stipulated by the Clause.
It is therefore contended that the petitioner is not entitled to claim the benefit of the said clause.
Exhibit R3(b) is another application for renewal submitted by the petitioner, which is dated 12.02.2014.
The said application is also not within the time stipulated by Clause-3.
Therefore, in any view of the matter, it is submitted that the petitioner is not entitled to claim the benefit of the said clause.
It is also contended that the petitioner has not satisfied the other conditions stipulated by the said clause.
4. Apart from the above, according to the third respondent, there are complaints against the manner in which the petitioner has been conducting the canteen and the light refreshment stall.
Exhibit R3(c) is a complaint made by the Head Vehicle Supervisor, Aluva on 31.07.2013 complaining of an incident where a piece of glass was found in the food that he was consuming.
He has stated in his complaint that, had he swallowed the piece of glass, the consequence would have been disastrous.

On Exhibit R3(c), an enquiry had been ordered and according to the counsel for the respondents,
the complaint was found to be true and the petitioner had been fined.
The report is Exhibit R3(d), by which a fine of 500/- was imposed on the petitioner.

Exhibit R3(f) is a communication of the third respondent to the Chief Traffic Officer that refers to the various incidents in which the food served in the petitioner's canteen was found to be deficient in many respects.

Considering all the above aspects, it has been decided not to renew the license of the petitioner and therefore, by the issue of Exhibit R3(i), tenders have been invited, for the purpose of auctioning the right to conduct the canteen.
The auction is scheduled to be held on 02.04.2014.
As per Exhibit R3(h) dated 17.03.02014, the petitioner has been informed that the renewal sought for by him was refused.
It was thereafter that the writ petition was filed, according to the counsel.

It is therefore contended that, the respondents are within their rights to refuse renewal of the license in respect of the canteen and no interference with the said proceedings is called for at the hands of this Court.
5.
The counsel for the petitioner on the other hand points out that, Exhibit R3(c) complaint was made on 31.07.2013.
Though allegations made in the complaint are serious warranting even criminal action against the petitioner, no such action has admittedly been initiated against him.

Referring to the endorsements made in the margin of Exhibit R3(c), it is pointed out by the counsel that, on 31.07.2013 itself, it had been decided by the authorities to levy a penalty of 500/- on the petitioner.
The endorsement was signed by the third respondent.
Though an enquiry was conducted as evident from Exhibit R3(d), no notice thereof was issued to the petitioner at any time, nor was he heard.
By Exhibit R3(e), he has been directed to pay a fine of 500/-.

With respect to Exhibit R3(f), it is pointed out by the counsel that though the said communication is dated 10.02.2014, reference is made therein to various incidents that took place on 12.02.2014, 18.02.2014 and 25.02.2014.
The said communication also seeks to withdraw an earlier communication dated 04.03.2014.
In spite of the request to withdraw the communication of 04.03.2014, Exhibit R3(h) shows the said communication as the reference while deciding not to renew the license of the petitioner.

The above discrepancies are relied upon by the counsel to contend that, the said proceedings have all been created subsequently in order to give an impression that, refusal to renew the licence of the petitioner was justified.

The conduct of the respondents in not initiating any action on the allegation that a glass piece had been found in the food served at the canteen is according to the counsel, a tell tale circumstance that points to the falsity of the allegation.

Therefore, the counsel seeks the issue of Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/
4 appropriate orders staying the conduct of the auction that is scheduled to be held on 02.04.2014.
6.

sentences.text: Heard.
It is not in dispute that, the petitioner is a licensee of the canteen and light refreshment stall.
It is also not in dispute that the licence was being renewed from year to year.

The terms and conditions subject to which the renewal of license was granted, according to the petitioner, is contained in Exhibit P5 but, according to the third respondent, Exhibit R3(a) is the memorandum that is applicable.
According to the third respondent, the licence of the petitioner had been renewed for the previous year in accordance with Exhibit R3(a).
The same is dated 05.04.2011 and had superseded Exhibit P5.
The petitioner was also well aware of the above fact, it is contended.

Since Exhibit R3(a) is dated 05.04.2011, I accept the contention of the third respondent that, it is the provisions thereof that should govern the manner in which the licence of the petitioner is to be renewed.
7. According to Clause- 3 of Exhibit R3(a), a licensee is entitled to seek renewal of the license in his favour, subject to the conditions stipulated therein.

The conditions stipulated are :-
1.The licensee should have complied with all the conditions of the agreement.
2.He should have remitted the license fee without default at the appropriate time.
3.He should be willing to pay license fee enhanced by 10% of the previous rate.
4.He should have applied for renewal of the license at least two months before the date of expiry of the period of licence.
It is also stipulated by Clause-3 that, auction proceedings shall not be initiated for the grant of license to a third party on any other grounds.
In the present case, according to the counsel for the respondents, the petitioner has not complied with two of the essential conditions.
The petitioner has not complied with all the conditions of the agreement that he has entered into with the respondents.
He has also not submitted his application for renewal within the time stipulated by the clause.

8. According to the counsel for the petitioner, clause 4 stipulates that persons who are not interested in renewing the license should inform the authorities regarding the said intention at least two months prior to the date of expiry of the period of licence.

Since no such information had been communicated by the petitioner to the authorities, the only presumption that was available to the respondents was that the petitioner was desirous of continuing the stall for a further period.
In view of the above, according to the counsel for the petitioner, the submission of his application for renewal on 04.03.2014 is in substantial compliance with the stipulation contained in Clause-3.

However, the above contention has to be considered in the light of the other allegations made against the petitioner also.
9. Exhibit R3(c) shows that a complaint had been made against the petitioner on 31.07.2013 by the Head Vehicle Supervisor alleging that a glass piece was found in the food that was served to him on the said date.

Of course, a perusal of Exhibit R3(c) shows that the third respondent has made an Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/
5 endorsement in the margin of the said complaint directing that the licensee be levied a penalty of 500/-, with a direction and to recover the same.

It can be presumed that the authority had taken the above decision, even before he had directed an enquiry into the incident on the same date as seen from the endorsement at the bottom of the same document.
However, it appears that an enquiry was conducted as evident from Exhibit R3(d) and that a penalty of 500/- was directed to be paid by the licensee as per Exhibit R3(e).

Even if it is presumed that the authorities had decided to penalise the petitioner before the enquiry, the fact remains that the entire incident had taken place in July,
2013 and has not been called in question by any person, till date.

To a pointed question from the Court as to whether the petitioner has paid a fine of 500/- that has been demanded by Exhibit R3(e), the counsel for the petitioner has not been able to give any answer one way or the other.
Therefore, the only presumption possible is that the amount must have been paid.
The said penalty cannot be said to be excessive or harsh.
However, the fact remains that the petitioner had accepted the said penalty, without questioning either the genuineness of the allegation made against him or the quantum of penalty imposed on him.
Exhibit R3(f) refers to certain other incidents also where the food served at the petitioner's canteen was found to be wanting in the standards expected, on the side of hygiene also.
Of course no incident of any authority under the Food Safety Act initiating action against the petitioner is available.
However, the respondents while deciding whether to grant renewal of licence to the petitioner or not, are certainly entitled to take such facts also into account.
The counsel for the petitioner has drawn my attention to the discrepancies in Exhibit R3(f).
It is seen that, in the body of the said communication, references are made to incidents that took place on 12.02.2014, 18.02.2014 and 25.02.2014.
The explanation of the counsel for the respondents is that the date in Exhibit R3(f) has been wrongly entered as 10.02.2014 instead of 10.03.2014.
The actual date is seen below the endorsement made against the seal bearing the word 'despatched'.
It is true that the date below the endorsement is 10.03.2014.
If the date is taken as 10.03.2014, the discrepancies pointed out in Exhibit R3(f) do not exist.
It is also pointed out by the counsel for the petitioner that no proceedings actually rejecting the application submitted by the petitioner has been issued.
The authorities have also not objected to his application at any time pointing out that it was not made within the time stipulated.
10. It is true that no communication specifically rejecting the application of the petitioner has been issued by the respondents.

But, Exhibit P3, Exhibits P4 as well as Exhibit R3(h) issued on the basis of the said communication have informed the petitioner in unmistakable terms that the authorities were not willing to renew the licence in favour of the petitioner.
Admittedly, the petitioner has not submitted his application for renewal within the time stipulated by Clause-3.
The contention of the respondents that the petitioner has not complied with all the conditions of the agreement also remains.
The complaints regarding the manner in which the petitioner had been conducting the canteen also cannot be discarded as baseless and untenable.
In addition is the fact that the petitioner is only a licensee from year to year who has no right to continue unless the license is renewed in his favour.
The right to have the license renewed is subject to the stipulations contained in Clause 3 of Exhibit R3(a).
I am not satisfied that there are sufficient grounds justifying an interference with the impugned proceedings.
For the above reasons, this writ petition fails and is accordingly dismissed.
It is made clear that I have not entered any findings on the correctness of the allegations made against the petitioner.
